description:
LOCATION: crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/memory.rs:75-77

CURRENT SHAPE:
    /// A simple string error for `MemoryBackend` failures.
    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub struct MemoryError(pub String);

CALLER CONTRACT PROBLEM:
1. No #[non_exhaustive]. Adding a second field (backtrace, source error,
   error_code, retry-after, etc.) is a breaking change for every caller
   doing `MemoryError("...".to_owned())` literal construction or pattern-
   matching the tuple position. Once the `memory` feature ships in 0.1.x,
   we cannot enrich the error type without a 0.2.x bump that breaks every
   downstream integration test / smoke test that constructs a fixture
   MemoryError directly.
2. `pub String` field. Callers can match on the exact string content:
       if let MemoryError(s) = e { if s == "deserialize ContactCard: ..."
   The string content is implementation-defined (different formats at
   memory.rs:362, 615, 623, 676), but nothing in the type signature or
   the docstring tells callers this. The next refactor that changes
   "deserialize {type}: {err}" to "failed to deserialize {type}: {err}"
   silently breaks any caller doing string-match logic.

WHAT CALLERS CANNOT DEPEND ON:
- Cannot pattern-match safely; the variant set is implicitly closed but
  not enforced.
- Cannot read the error context programmatically — only via Display
  format-string parsing.

RECOMMENDED:
- Add #[non_exhaustive] at the struct level.
- Make the String field private; expose `as_str(&self) -> &str` and
  optionally `kind(&self) -> ErrorKind` for typed matching.
- Document that the Display content is implementation-defined and may
  change across minor versions.

NOTE: the canonical sibling jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs:449-452 has
the same problem (pub String, no #[non_exhaustive]). Per the workspace
canonical-template propagation rule, fixing the canonical and then this
crate is the correct ordering. File the canonical fix as a separate
bead; this finding scopes the contacts-server symptom.

The same shape problem exists for MockError (test_support module) but
that type is in a `pub(crate) mod test_support` so it does not appear
on the published API surface — out of scope.
title: memory::MemoryError missing #[non_exhaustive] and exposes pub String — adding context is a breaking change
